title: Why Investors Choose Genstone Construction
metaDescription: Why investors renovate with Genstone: no upfront payment, draws tied to completed work, vetted local contractors, permits and lien waivers handled.
lede: An investor renovation needs more than a construction estimate. It needs a scope tied to the asset, the budget and the plan for the property, a payment structure that protects your cash, and enough visibility that you can manage the job without standing in the kitchen every afternoon. These are the six reasons investors, lenders and funds bring their properties to Genstone Construction.

sections.h2: Scopes written around the investment, not just the house
sections.body:
Most contractors price what they see. An investor needs a contractor who prices what the deal requires. Genstone develops detailed project scopes around the asset, the budget and the investment strategy, so you understand the renovation priorities before any work begins.

Where appropriate, we also develop renovation options aligned with the projected ARV, the budget available and the intended use of the property. On a flip, that might mean one plan that brings the house up to the level of the average renovated comp and another that pushes toward the top of the neighborhood, with the cost difference spelled out. On a rental, it might mean comparing a cosmetic refresh against a plan that also replaces an aging furnace and water heater so the first years of the hold are quieter.

The scope document and estimate lay out labor, materials and the draw schedule. That gives you something concrete to compare against your pro forma, share with a lender or partner, and hold the project to once it starts.

There are no upfront payments. Construction draws are tied to completed work, and final payment is due only after the project is complete and you've approved it.

For investors, that structure does real work. Your capital stays available for the purchase, closing costs, carrying costs and reserves until it's actually needed. You aren't exposed to the situation every experienced investor has heard about at least once, where a large deposit goes out, a crew shows up for a few days, and then the job stalls. And because draws release against finished stages, the payment schedule tends to fit the way investor rehab loans fund, which is also against completed and inspected work.

The draw schedule is set out in the estimate before the job starts, so you know in advance which milestones trigger which payments. Dumpster and debris removal costs are already included in the estimate, rather than showing up as a surprise line on a later invoice.

Genstone coordinates a network of thousands of licensed and insured contractors. The people on site in each market are vetted local contractors who know the area's houses, suppliers and building department. The scoping, project management, documentation and billing around them follow national standards set by Genstone's team in Romeoville, Illinois.

That combination matters most to investors who own, or plan to own, in more than one place. A portfolio spread across several cities can still have one scope format, one draw process and one way of reporting progress. It also matters to institutional clients. Genstone works for mortgage servicers, REITs, investment funds, banks with REO inventory and other mortgage lenders, and is a preferred contractor for Government-Sponsored Enterprises. Those clients need consistent documentation across a large number of properties, and the same systems support an individual investor with a single house.

Local execution also means the crew isn't learning the market on your project. Older housing stock in one city and newer slab-on-grade construction in another call for different trades and different assumptions, and local contractors bring that knowledge to the job.

sections.h2: Risk management built into every project
sections.body:
Renovation risk isn't only about cost overruns. Unpermitted work can surface at resale or refinance. A subcontractor who wasn't paid can file a lien against your property. An uninsured worker injured on site can become your problem. Missing documentation can hold up a lender's draw or an institutional client's reporting.

Genstone builds permitting, inspections, lien waivers, contractor compliance and documentation into every project. Contractors assigned to Genstone projects are verified for appropriate insurance and applicable licensing. Required permits and inspections are coordinated as part of project management. Lien waivers are collected as part of the payment process, which helps keep the title clean when you sell or refinance. Photos and records are kept as the job moves, so there's a trail for your lender, your partners or your own files.

None of this is glamorous, and investors rarely ask about it on the first call. It tends to come up later, at the closing table or during an appraisal, and that's when having it done right pays off.

You can track progress, documentation and project milestones without needing to be on site. Each project has a designated field manager or project manager who serves as your main point of contact from start to finish, oversees execution and handles issues as they come up.

For investors who live in a different city from their properties, or who are running several projects at once, that visibility is often the difference between a renovation you can manage and one you have to babysit. You see what was completed, what's next and what changed, with photos and documentation attached.

When something unexpected turns up behind a wall or under a floor, you hear about it with the information you need to decide: what was found, what it affects and what it would cost to address. Approved changes are documented before additional work proceeds, so the scope on paper and the work in the house stay the same.

We understand the numbers behind every renovation decision and help align scope, budget and execution with your investment strategy. That's where the work starts, with the free Pre-Offer Rehab Review: an estimate of repair costs, a refined look at the ARV, and a check on whether the numbers support your offer before your capital is committed.

The review exists because the most expensive renovation mistakes happen before closing. An offer written on an optimistic rehab number, or on an ARV that assumes finishes the neighborhood won't pay for, leaves no room to recover once you own the property.

The executive team has more than 60 years of combined construction experience, with deep roots in REO, fix-and-flip projects and single-family remodeling. The broader team includes estimators, field managers, repair specialists and billing staff, each focused on a different part of keeping an investor project on budget and on schedule.

sections.h2: Quality workmanship at the right finish level
sections.body:
Quality for an investor means professional, market-appropriate finishes designed around the property's intended use and investment strategy. It does not mean the most expensive materials in the catalog.

On a flip, the finishes have to match or beat the renovated comps a buyer will tour that same weekend. On a rental, they have to hold up to move-ins, move-outs and years of daily use, and be easy to repair or match when something gets damaged. On a property headed for a refinance, they have to support the value the appraiser needs to see. Getting that level right is part of the job, and so is the installation itself: straight tile lines, tight trim, properly sealed wet areas and work that passes inspection the first time.

Completed work carries a one-year workmanship warranty. Damage caused by tenants and normal wear and tear aren't covered. Genstone's work has been recognized with Best of Houzz 2025 for Service, and the company has been named to the Inc. 5000 list of America's fastest-growing private companies two years in a row.

sections.h2: The kinds of work we take on
sections.body: Genstone Construction renovates fix and flip properties, BRRRR projects, single-family rentals, small multifamily buildings of two to four units, REO and bank-owned homes, FHA 203(k) projects and rental turns. Genstone is an FHA 203(k) Certified Contractor and is part of the Genstone Companies, which also include Genstone Realty, Genstone Financial, Genstone Insurance, Genstone Property Management, Genstone Field Services and Title Clearing & Escrow. That means a renovation can be connected to the financing, insurance, management and title work around it when the deal calls for it.
